message:
Hi Usman, thanks for the detailed proposal! Your technical background and emphasis on DFMA and GD&T really
stood out. A lot of freelancers just send quick renders, but I need something that can actually be manufactured
reliably.

To answer your questions:
Manufacturing Process: The final product will be plastic injection molded (ABS or PC/ABS blend), but we need
to 3D print (FDM/SLA) functional prototypes first to test the mechanism. So the design needs to be optimized for
injection molding, but easily printable for testing.
Internal Hardware: Yes, we have a custom PCB (approx 65mm x 40mm x 12mm), a 18650 Li-ion battery holder,
a small servo motor, and a internal latch mechanism.
Operating Environment: Handheld consumer device, indoor/light outdoor use. Needs drop protection (1.2m drop
test resistance) and clean ergonomics.

And My budget for this initial CAD and manufacturing prep milestone is $200. Can we cover the main housing 3D CAD,
internal mounting features, basic tolerance check, and initial drawing set within this budget?

Hi Areeba,
Thank you for the detailed information. The requirements are clear, and the combination of injection molding for production and FDM/SLA printing for prototype validation is a practical approach.

Yes, I can cover the main housing CAD, internal mounting features for the PCB, battery holder, and servo integration, along with an initial tolerance review and drawing package within the $200 budget.

For this phase, I would deliver:

• Complete 3D CAD model of the housing and internal structure
• PCB, battery, and hardware mounting features
• Production ready STEP files for prototyping and manufacturing review
• Initial engineering drawings with key dimensions and assembly details
• Basic DFM review for injection molding, including wall thickness, draft angles, and assembly considerations

Once the design is reviewed and tested through prototypes, we can make any necessary refinements before moving toward final manufacturing documentation.

If you can share the PCB files, dimensions, and any available mechanical references, I can review everything and get started right away.

Usman, that breakdown is excellent. Exactly what I was looking for. I really appreciate you breaking down the DFM
feedback report and draft analysis—that will save us thousands in tooling adjustments down the line.
I have attached the DXF file for the PCB board outline, along with a rough hand sketch of the latch layout and overall
aesthetic preference.

Let's set up the contract for $200 with the deliverables you outlined above. What is your estimated timeline to
complete this stage?

Great! Thank you for the update.

Before I begin, I noticed that the DXF, hand sketch, and reference pictures you mentioned don't seem to have come through on my end. Could you please resend the files when you have a moment? Once I receive them, I'll review everything and get started right away.

**Project Timeline (3 Business Days)**

**Day 1**
• Develop the overall 3D architecture
• Verify PCB and battery fitment
• Create the primary enclosure shell in SolidWorks

**Day 2**
• Design the internal latch mechanism
• Add ribs, bosses, and mounting features
• Perform draft angle analysis and tolerance checks
• Share progress screenshots/3D views for your review

**Day 3**
• Finalize the CAD model
• Generate STEP files
• Prepare 2D engineering drawings with BOM and key dimensions
• Complete the DFM review
• Deliver the final project package

Please go ahead and send the Upwork offer for the $200 milestone. Once the milestone is funded and I receive the project files, I’ll get started immediately.

Great! I’ve received the files and reviewed them.

Everything looks clear, and now I have what I need to move forward with the design. I’ll begin with the overall 3D architecture, PCB/battery fitment, and enclosure setup, then move on to the internal mechanism and manufacturability review.

Awesome, Usman! I've just officially sent over the Upwork contract offer for $200.00 with Milestone 1 funded
("SolidWorks 3D CAD, DFMA Optimization & Engineering Drawing Package").
Looking forward to working together and seeing the initial CAD models!
I Apologize for the delay. There was some issue with the payment method, that's why I couldn't send the offer

Hi Areeba,

Thank you! I've accepted the offer and will begin working on the project right away. I'll keep you updated on the progress and deliver the work as soon as possible.
